explain.title: How this economy works
explain.cpi.body: The average of every item's price compared to its starting price. 110 means things cost 10% more than when the market opened.
explain.inflation.body: How fast the price index is rising, per day. A little inflation is normal; a lot means money is losing value quickly.
explain.rate.body: The central bank raises the loan rate when prices rise too fast or trade overheats, and lowers it in a slump.
explain.liquidity.body: Selling to the market creates new money. When inflation runs hot, payouts are trimmed slightly so less new money appears.
explain.priceLevel.body: When players hold more money each — from jobs, drops or rewards — base prices rise with it, so the market can't be bought out with cheap money.
explain.treasury.body: Market taxes and loan interest are saved in a server treasury instead of disappearing.
explain.stabilizers.body: Taxes drop when trading slows down and rise when it booms, smoothing out the ups and downs.
explain.ubi.body: Part of the treasury's surplus is shared among online players, more generously during a recession.
explain.wealthTax.body: Very large balances pay a small daily tax, only on the part above each threshold.
explain.reversion.body: Items bought out slowly come back into supply, and flooded items slowly get used up, so prices drift back toward normal.
explain.spillovers.body: Items in the same category, and substitutes like cod and salmon, move a little together.
explain.recipes.body: A crafted item's price stays close to the cost of its ingredients.
explain.spread.body: While a price is swinging wildly, buying and selling get a slightly wider gap to discourage quick flips.
explain.shocks.body: Now and then a shortage, glut, boom or slump pushes prices for a few hours, then fades.
